question: Which benchmarks and datasets exist for causal discovery and causal reasoning, where does each one's ground truth come from, what does it score, and how can it leak?

schema.name: benchmark or dataset collection; projects sharing a name are separate rows
schema.category: structure / time series / root cause / representation / simulator / platform / LLM reasoning / agentic
schema.ground_truth_origin: synthetic generator / LLM-written / expert-elicited / physical system / experimental / literature-curated (mixed allowed)
schema.regimes: D observational data given, I interventional data given (bool or text), K_names: are names meaningful
schema.interventional_data: bool; null = not stated in pages read
schema.hidden_confounders: bool or text; null = not stated
schema.known_leaks: list of {leak, evidence, label (reported / measured (project) / second-hand / inference), sources}
schema.memorisation_risk: {level, why}; level is this audit's judgment
schema.used_by: systems or papers reporting on it
schema.sources: URLs read 2026-10-12, plus prior-note: or project: pointers where a fact comes from an earlier project note

rows.name: CausalArena (generated families: synthetic, semantic, formula)
rows.ground_truth_origin: synthetic generator (synthetic family); LLM-written with human review (semantic and formula families: 'staged agentic workflow' with 'Human and LLM-assisted' review)
rows.variables: semantic 17-25 vars, 25-67 edges (paper); public semantic 17-25 vars, 26-67 edges (project)
rows.samples: 1,000 obs rows, or 800 obs + 200 int rows; 5 replicates per scenario

regimes.K_names: semantic and formula: named (node_id like 'agitation_rpm', labels like 'calibration drift bias'); synthetic: anonymous

rows.metrics: directed-edge precision/recall/F1, SHD; replicate then family averaging; undirected PC/GIES edges oriented at random (Appendix B per project)

known_leaks.evidence: Every true edge runs from an earlier to a later column in every released file checked (semantic 2,068/2,068; formula 1,714/1,714; synthetic 50,421/50,421). Naive regression on earlier columns: 0.680 directed F1 on public semantic files vs 0.269 after shuffle; 0.575 on formula. The paper does not discuss column order.
known_leaks.label: measured (project)

known_leaks.evidence: Causal-Copilot final F1 0.306 with real names, 0.232 neutral, 0.142 names swapped between columns.
known_leaks.label: measured (project)

known_leaks.evidence: Semantic SCMs come from an agentic drafting workflow with LLM-assisted review; directions an LLM finds plausible are therefore over-represented relative to a world-sampled graph. No test of this in the paper.
known_leaks.label: reported (construction) + inference (consequence)

known_leaks.evidence: Paper cites UUMC as a way to reduce sortability but does not describe CausalArena's own handling or report varsortability.
known_leaks.label: reported

known_leaks.evidence: Authors name public SCMs entering pretraining as the main leakage concern; plan versioning and a held-out half.
known_leaks.label: reported

known_leaks.evidence: Replay sampler intervenes only on declared targets, round-robin; one inspected spec: 5 targets, all roots.
known_leaks.label: second-hand (prior note, V there)

memorisation_risk.why: Public half released Sept 2026 under CC BY 4.0 on Hugging Face; scenarios are new, but named graphs were drafted by LLMs so a name-reading model recovers LLM-plausible edges even without memorisation.

rows.maintained: v1 Sept 2026; held-out half reserved for later versions
used_by: CausalArena paper (18 methods incl. FoundCause, GIES, CDFM, TabCausal, PC)
rows.notes: Public: 50 of 100 semantic, 50 formula, 500 synthetic configs (project). No agent or LLM entries on leaderboard (prior note).

rows.task: cause-to-effect and effect-to-cause, with and without intervention (text, math, code)
rows.ground_truth_origin: not stated on page

rows.name: CRAB (Romanou et al., EMNLP 2023)
rows.ground_truth_origin: expert/annotator-labelled (method not stated on page)

memorisation_risk.why: News events of 2022-ish are in training data.

rows.name: e-CARE (Du et al., ACL 2022)
rows.ground_truth_origin: human-annotated

rows.name: COPA (Roemmele, Bejan, Gordon 2011)
rows.ground_truth_origin: expert-written (creation details not on page)

rows.name: Kıcıman et al. LLM causal evaluations (Tübingen-LLM, neuropathic, counterfactual, actual causality)
rows.task: pairwise orientation from names; counterfactual; event causality
rows.ground_truth_origin: reuses Tübingen pairs, neuropathic simulator, CRASS-type vignettes

known_leaks.evidence: Row-completion recall 61% of cells / 25% of rows; authors argue memorisation alone does not explain accuracy and test post-cutoff data.
known_leaks.label: second-hand (prior note) + reported abstract

rows.name: CausalQuest / Quriosity (Ceraolo et al.)
rows.task: identify causal questions among natural user queries
rows.ground_truth_origin: naturally occurring questions; labelling method not stated
rows.maintained: IJCNLP-AACL 2025 Findings (abs page now titled Quriosity)
rows.notes: The abs page for arXiv 2405.20318 titles it Quriosity; equating it with CausalQuest rests on my recollection of the ID.

rows.name: CaLM (Chen et al.)
rows.ground_truth_origin: curated mix (construction not stated on page)

rows.name: CLEAR (Chen et al.)
rows.ground_truth_origin: synthetic graph tasks (construction not detailed)

rows.name: CausalGraph2LLM (Sheth et al.)
rows.task: graph-level and node-level causal queries given an encoded graph
rows.ground_truth_origin: graphs not listed on page

known_leaks.evidence: GPT-4 and Gemini-1.5 deviate by about 60% across graph encodings; contextual information triggers parametric-memory bias.
known_leaks.label: reported

rows.maintained: arXiv v2 Feb 2025 (NAACL Findings 2025 per search result)

rows.name: CRASS (Frohberg & Binder)
rows.ground_truth_origin: hand-built with crowd-validated human baseline

rows.name: Feng et al. 2025 occurrence-controlled probes (ConceptNet, CauseNet pairs; fictitious-term relations)
rows.task: pair direction; full discovery on small medical/Arctic/insurance graphs
rows.ground_truth_origin: literature/knowledge-base pairs plus synthetic fictitious relations injected into Dolma docs

regimes.K_names: named; fictitious names for the control

known_leaks.evidence: OLMo full-discovery F1 falls from 0.88 (highest pretraining occurrence) to 0.2 (lowest).
known_leaks.label: reported

memorisation_risk.why: Uses open-corpus models to count exposure directly.

rows.notes: The only design found that measures exposure in the pretraining corpus directly.

rows.name: CARE probe protocol (Dong et al.) on bnlearn
rows.task: LLM structure discovery with original / random / permuted names, N in {0,50,200}, +/- algorithm output
rows.ground_truth_origin: expert-elicited bnlearn graphs (Asia, Survey, Earthquake, Alarm)

known_leaks.evidence: Performance collapses when names are random or permuted; more data helps little.
known_leaks.label: reported

rows.notes: Column reordering used only as augmentation, not a measured factor (prior note).

rows.name: CausalDS (Leban & Sun)
rows.task: end-to-end data-science causal tasks (rungs 1-3) in a sandbox
rows.ground_truth_origin: synthetic generator (hidden sampled SCM) with a synthetic story; optional grounding in real distributions
rows.variables: small motifs (IV, confounding, front-door, chain, grafted)
rows.hidden_confounders: confounding motifs; non-identifiable tasks imply unobserved confounding (inference)
rows.metrics: pass rate; identification-gated effect tasks; abstention scored; interval score and coverage

known_leaks.evidence: Natural-language stories carry names; prior note says a verbalisation swap was used (not re-verified).
known_leaks.label: second-hand

used_by: 7 frontier models (Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5 82.4% pass, prior note)

rows.name: CauSciBench (Acharya et al., ICML 2026)
rows.ground_truth_origin: literature-curated (replicated papers, textbooks) plus synthetic
rows.metrics: method-selection accuracy, relative error of estimate

known_leaks.evidence: Real-paper queries have published estimates a model may recall (inference).
known_leaks.label: inference

rows.name: CausalReasoningBenchmark (Sawarni, Tan, Syrgkanis)
rows.task: identification spec + estimate from real data
rows.ground_truth_origin: literature-curated from 73 papers and 3 textbooks
rows.metrics: identification spec scored field by field; estimate scored separately

known_leaks.evidence: Gold estimates come from published work (inference).
known_leaks.label: inference

rows.name: CausalVerify (Zhang et al.)
rows.ground_truth_origin: mixed: 259 real-paper contexts, 100 synthetic scenarios with executable references, paper-twin pairs
rows.metrics: joint recovery of estimate and SE; four layers

known_leaks.evidence: On the two newest pairs the gain appeared only for models from the family that built the references.
known_leaks.label: reported

rows.notes: Direct evidence that LLM-built references favour the same model family.

rows.name: QRData (Liu et al., Findings ACL 2024)
rows.task: statistical and causal QA with data
rows.ground_truth_origin: literature-curated (textbooks, course material, papers)

rows.name: DiscoveryBench (Majumder et al.)
rows.ground_truth_origin: literature-curated workflows from papers (real) plus synthetic

rows.name: CausalPitfalls (Du et al.)
rows.ground_truth_origin: authored challenges with rubrics
rows.metrics: rubric scored by validated LLM judge

rows.name: InterveneBench (Shi et al.)
rows.ground_truth_origin: literature-curated (744 social-science studies)

rows.name: Active Causal Discovery Benchmark (ACDB; Deb, Shah, Krishnan)
rows.task: structure with budgeted hard interventions (observe-intervene-submit API)
rows.ground_truth_origin: synthetic generator (linear-Gaussian)

regimes.K_names: node indices permuted 'so names do not leak topology' (prior note)

rows.metrics: directed F1, SHD, intervention efficiency; skeleton/DAG/efficiency layers; random-DAG floor 23.6%

known_leaks.leak: varsortability / R2-sortability of simulated additive-noise data
known_leaks.evidence: Generic ANM simulations have varsortability above 0.94 (linear) and R2-sortability about 0.8 by default; sort-and-regress baselines match continuous methods; R2-sortability survives standardisation (reported in Reisach 2021/2023, via prior note; abstracts re-read today). Not measured for this specific generator.
known_leaks.label: reported (general), unmeasured for this row

rows.name: CausaLab (Yang et al.)
rows.ground_truth_origin: synthetic generator (randomly sampled hidden SCM)

known_leaks.evidence: GPT-5.2-high: 92% task accuracy but 0.471 edge F1 observational at 6 nodes.
known_leaks.label: reported

rows.name: CausalGame (Chen et al.)
rows.task: AI-scientist game with selection bias, measurement error, hidden confounders
rows.ground_truth_origin: synthetic SCM-driven game

rows.name: BoxingGym (Gandhi et al.)
rows.ground_truth_origin: probabilistic models from science
rows.metrics: expected information gain, explanation-based prediction, prediction error

rows.name: Auto-Discovery-Bench (Chen et al.)
rows.ground_truth_origin: synthetic oracle

rows.name: ReplaySCM (Batzoglou)
rows.task: induce executable Boolean mechanisms from interventions
rows.ground_truth_origin: synthetic generator (Boolean SCMs)

regimes.K_names: order disclosure varied: Ordered / Block-order / Hidden-order / Hidden-roots

known_leaks.evidence: Held-out replay drops sharply when order or roots are hidden.
known_leaks.label: reported

rows.notes: Only benchmark found that varies causal-order disclosure as a factor.
